The Eco-Plant model is applied by palynologists for palaeoenvironmental reconstructions using dispersed sporomorphs from the Cenozoic (e.g., [16–19]) and Mesozoic (e.g., [3,20–27]). However, for most of the Mesozoic dispersed sporomorphs, the application of Eco-Plant is limited, because either their assignment to a specific Eco-Plant remains uncertain or the botanical affinities to plant taxa are unclear [3]. For the dispersed Mesozoic sporomorph genera of Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, and Gymnosperms [30], which are included in the database, their EPH and EPT are stored in dataset Ecogroup (Table 2). The dispersed sporomorphs of angiosperms are currently not linked to Eco-Plant. Nevertheless, the first reliable angiosperm is discovered at the top of the Jurassic [87–88]. Therefore, this database is capable of automatically linking all sporomorph genera from the Triassic and the Jurassic to Eco-Plant to reconstruct relative climate changes. However, the terms used by different authors for Eco-Plant groups are not always the same, making the comparison of results between different authors difficult, e.g., the Thermophytic form used by Wang et al. [20] is more or less the same as the Megathermic element used by Suc and Fauquette [19]. The term Halophytes is equivocal [89] and it is difficult to distinguish this Eco-Plant group from Xerophytes. Therefore, most authors (e.g., [20,22]) use the term Xerophytes to represent both Halophytes and Xerophytes in the Mesozoic. In this database, the concept of Eco-Plant groups that assess the effect of humidity (EPH) and the effect of temperature (EPT) follows Zhang et al. [3] and Zhang [30], which makes it easier to compare the results between different users using the same concepts. Users can also review published sporomorph data by extracting them from published studies and by uploading these data to the database.

steps.title: Create upload CSV file
steps.instruction: Prepare a CSV file that follows the required format: include exactly three columns named Sample, Genus, and Abundance (field names may be lower‑case, upper‑case or mixed‑case). The Sample column holds sample identifiers, the Genus column holds sporomorph genus names, and the Abundance column may contain either raw grain counts or percentage values. Save the file with a .csv extension.

steps.title: Open the Sporopollen web interface
steps.instruction: Navigate to the analysis page at http://www.sporopollen.com/sporemesozoicsegs.php?opencode=paper1. For guidance and example files, also open the manual page at http://www.sporopollen.com/sporeexample.php?opterate=Paleoenvironmental%20Reconstruction.

steps.title: Upload the CSV dataset
steps.instruction: Click the “Choose File” button (Fig. 1‑A) and select the prepared CSV file from the local computer. The button label may appear in the local language (e.g., Chinese characters) on non‑English systems.

steps.title: Select analysis mode
steps.instruction: From the drop‑down list (Fig. 1‑B) choose one of the available modes:

substeps.instruction: Vegetation Family, Vegetation Order, or Vegetation Phylum – links genera to parent plant families, orders or phyla.
Eco‑Plant EPH or Eco‑Plant EPT – links genera to humidity (EPH) or temperature (EPT) groups.
Any of the above followed by “PDF” – produces a graphical diagram instead of a numeric table.
Draw Curve PDF – plots the uploaded data directly without linking to the database.

steps.title: Prepare special file for Draw Curve mode (if chosen)
steps.instruction: If the “Draw Curve PDF” mode is selected, the uploaded CSV must follow the Table 5 format: the first column is Sample, and each subsequent column is a plant‑group (e.g., Bennettitales, Cheirolepidiaceae, etc.) containing percentage abundances. Save this file as a CSV before uploading.

steps.title: Submit the job
steps.instruction: Click the “Submit” button (Fig. 1‑D). The server (MySQL + PHP) will receive the file, store it as the temporary dataset “Uploaded”, link it to the appropriate reference dataset (Taxonomy for vegetation modes, Ecogroup for Eco‑Plant modes, or none for Draw Curve), calculate abundances by grouping on Sample and the selected taxonomic or eco‑climatic field, and generate the result.

substeps.instruction: For non‑PDF modes: a result table (e.g., Table 4) showing percentages of the selected group per sample; genera without known affinity are labeled “Uncertain”.
For PDF modes: a diagram comparable to a pollen diagram (Fig. 3) displaying the same percentage data graphically.
For Draw Curve PDF: a diagram plotted directly from the uploaded percentages.
